\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پکوڑا} (pakoṛā)}{پکوڑا (pakoṛā)}]{\ur{پکوڑا} (pakoṛā) — a pakora}

\label{lesson:UR-C200-pakora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for turmeric, then the Urdu for cumin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پکوڑا}}
\textbf{\ur{پکوڑا}} — \emph{pakoṛā} — \textquotedblleft{}a pakora\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پکوڑا}} (\emph{pakoṛā}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*pakvavaṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}cooked ball\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 7625). It is built from \emph{pakva}, \textquotedblleft{}cooked\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{vaṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}a round cake\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pakoṛā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pakoṛā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{pakoṛā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for turmeric, then the Urdu for cumin, then say \emph{pakoṛā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پکوڑا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pakora\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{cousinweb}

It is built from \emph{rājikā}, \textquotedblleft{}mustard\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{tikta}, \textquotedblleft{}bitter\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
